content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'hotshot-gpu-02' p99 latency breach > 6s for the last 5m. Autoscaler lag detected. Queue depth: 420 (threshold 200). Impact: streaming stalls reported. Paging maya. :rotating_light:

maya: oncall here, joining. seeing p95 ~ 1.4s, p99 ~ 6.2s on streaming route /v1/stream. Any active deploys?

raj: no deploys I know. I pulled the autoscaler logs: `autoscaler: heartbeat delayed 38s`, scale requests queued. Looks like many warmup handshakes failing.

eli: warmup metrics look odd — GPU init rate got throttled by our init-rate limiter after burst. Warmup concurrency hit the safety cap. Warmup backlog ~ 160.

maya: customer-impact check — support reported 3 customers complaining about stalls, CS flagged one enterprise trial in EU region. Sara, can you confirm?

sara: yep, CS says customers saw multiple streaming cutouts and reconnects between 12:08-12:14 UTC. Severity = S2 for now. Not yet widespread but visible on paid tiers.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily raise warmup concurrency cap for this pool 2) manually scale pool by +4 slots 3) enable fallback routing to smaller quantized model for streaming route to reduce tail tokens. Raj/eli — who can run steps 1/2?

raj: I can do manual scaleup now. Running: `redwoodctl pool scale hotshot-gpu-02 --add 4 --now`

support-bot: deploy started by raj at 2026-03-15T12:16:10Z. Request id abc123.

eli: I'll flip the warmup cap: `PATCH /config/warmup?pool=hotshot-gpu-02` set `max_concurrency=80` (was 40). Doing it now.

maya: taylor — can you toggle fallback routing? We want streaming to prefer q4-small model if warmup not complete. Should be a quick route config change.

taylor: on it. Changing routing policy: set prefer_tier=cheap-quantized for route /v1/stream with fallback_time_ms=2000. `routes.update(...)` done.

maya: good. raj — any ETA on additional slots coming online?

raj: scale API returned success, new slots provisioning. ETA estimated warmup 45-90s per slot (GPU boot + load). Seeing first slot READY at 12:18:05 UTC.

eli: monitoring: queue depth dropped from 420 -> 210 after warmup cap bump and route change. p99 improved to ~3.8s within 3m. Still taily but trending down.

incident-bot: Note: autoscaler has a backlog of pending scale decisions. Heartbeat jitter correlated with control-plane GC around 12:05 UTC, see gc-log-20260315-1204.

maya: root-cause hypothesis: short control-plane GC spike caused autoscaler heartbeat delay, combined with strict warmup concurrency cap and a sudden customer burst -> warmup queue amplified -> p99 breach. Correct?

raj: yes. Also observed that our warmup init-rate limiter doesn't respect prioritization for streaming-heavy routes — it throttles all warmups equally. That amplified customer-facing latency.

sara: customer-impact update: one enterprise had 4 reconnections but recovered after 12:20 UTC. We'll notify CS to send an interim note.

maya: next actions (short): 1) make warmup cap bump temporary (rollback after traffic normalizes) 2) add priority override for streaming routes in warmup scheduler 3) investigate control-plane GC bump and autoscaler resilience (postmortem). Anyone object?

eli: agree. I'll open a runtime ticket for adding priority flags to warmup scheduler and a canary for init-rate limiter.

raj: I'll follow up with infra to correlate GC events and autoscaler heartbeats. Also propose we add a soft-handoff that allows immediate partial responses via fallback model while warmup completes (short-term mitigation).

taylor: I'll add a dashboard widget for warmup queue depth by pool and route, and an alert if queue > 150 for >2m.

sara: CS note: drafting customer message. Will wait 30m and then send status update.

maya: oncall status: I'll own live mitigation until 12:45 UTC then handoff to raj for postmortem. If anything regresses ping me directly.

support-bot: scale finished: all 4 new slots READY at 2026-03-15T12:19:30Z.

eli: post-mitigations: p95 ~1.1s, p99 ~2.6s, queue depth steady at 40. Logging capture saved at s3://redwood-incident-logs/1794512345/ for postmortem.

maya: thanks team. Recording this thread for postmortem. Escalating to oncall schedule: raj will take lead on RCA. I'll mark incident S2 -> will update if severity changes.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated (partial). Pager cleared at 12:20:50 UTC.

maya: handoff to raj for RCA/debrief. raj, you have the pen.

raj: got it. I'll collect telemetry, warmup traces, and autoscaler logs and start a postmortem doc. Expected timeline: draft within 48h.

maya: closing live mitigation thread, leaving any further notes to raj. :thumbsup:
